details.description: Fireworks AI documents fireworks-asr-v2, branded 'Streaming ASR v2,' as a preview of its next-generation real-time speech transcription model, offering lower latency plus cross-region and cross-cloud support compared with Streaming ASR v1, over the same WebSocket-based streaming API. Fireworks' archived model page, captured January 15, 2026, lists it as 'Ready' for serverless use and created September 24, 2025, but does not publish a parameter count, context length, or accuracy figures. As of this research date, the dedicated model page for fireworks-asr-v2 no longer resolves on fireworks.ai (it returns HTTP 404), so whether it has since left preview could not be confirmed on a live page.
advantages: Fireworks describes it as offering lower latency than Streaming ASR v1, plus cross-region and cross-cloud support, per its archived model page.
disadvantages: Documented by Fireworks as a preview version as of the most recent available capture of its model page (January 2026); whether it has since reached general availability could not be confirmed on a live page.
Fireworks' model page did not publish a parameter count, context length, or accuracy/WER figures for this model.

The dedicated fireworks.ai model page for this model returns HTTP 404 as of the research date, and Fireworks' current documentation index has no dedicated audio-transcription API page, so current availability and status could not be confirmed on a live source.
use_cases: Real-time transcription of live audio over a WebSocket connection, particularly where lower latency or cross-region/cross-cloud routing matters.

sources.title: Streaming ASR v2 (fireworks-asr-v2) | Fireworks AI Model Library -- Wayback Machine capture, 2026-01-15
Real-Time Speech Recognition for Enterprise Voice AI | Fireworks

notes: The live fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/fireworks-asr-v2 page returns HTTP 404 as of 2026-09-24 (verified directly with repeated requests) and has no Wayback Machine snapshot after 2026-01-15, so that January capture -- which itself labeled the model a 'preview' -- was used as the primary source; current status could not be confirmed on a live maker page. Fireworks' current speech-recognition landing page (fetched live) describes generic 'streaming and pre-recorded audio SKUs' and names Whisper/Whisper Turbo, not fireworks-asr-v2 by name. Bud's catalog lists this model under the /v1/audio/transcriptions REST endpoint, while Fireworks documented it as a WebSocket-based streaming transcription API; I did not attempt to resolve this difference. No accuracy/WER or language-coverage figures were found for this specific model.
